newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA says interest rates should hold.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA says interest rates should hold.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) managing director David Murray said on Sunday that indications of a pickup in business investment activity should mean interest rates will hold steady for the time being.

While the Christmas period had not been good for all retailers, "our indicators show steady improvement on a lot of factors that are indicative of a buildup in activity during 1997", Murray said in an interview on the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.
"And for that reason we're more inclined to think that the interest rates might hold," he said.
CBA is one of Australia's "big four" national banks which are major lenders to the business and housing sectors.

The Reserve Bank of Australia, the nation's central bank, last changed the official cash rate on December 11, when it announced a 50 basis point reduction to 6.0 percent, the last of three cuts since July 1996.

RBA governor Ian Macfarlane said last week any further changes in rates would probably have to wait for the outcome of the current "living wage" case being heard by the national wage tribunal but also noted that recent rate cuts were having a favourable impact on investment and employment.
The Australian government has forecast economic growth of 3.5 percent in 1996/97, with the strength driven by a business investment surge.
